controls.reason: Review and test records are bounded, but whether security analysis is substantive and the test scope is adequate requires expert judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A change can carry three approval artifacts while its security review is superficial and misses a new public exposure.

controls.reason: A versioned infrastructure record can require documented resource quotas, account limits and provider limits with units and scope identities.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An account or resource class missing one of the three limit records fails the finite schema.

controls.reason: Detecting all drift, unauthorized resources and shadow infrastructure requires a complete authoritative estate and discovery coverage.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Configured scans can be green while an out-of-band account contains an unknown public resource.

controls.reason: A recovery-procedure document and test run do not prove recovery across all resource types, deletion modes and recreated dependencies.
controls.counterexample_analysis: One scripted recreation can pass while deletion of a stateful dependency loses data or identity bindings.

controls.reason: Topology records cannot prove multi-zone and multi-region behavior meets availability and recovery objectives during real correlated failures.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The approved architecture can span regions while a shared control plane prevents failover within the objective.

controls.reason: A bounded failure load test does not prove infrastructure capacity under all relevant failure domains, workloads and scaling states.
controls.counterexample_analysis: One zone-loss test can pass while simultaneous throttling makes remaining capacity insufficient.

controls.reason: Integration presence cannot prove all provider status and escalation paths are current, reachable and operational during incidents.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A status feed and phone tree can exist while an indirect provider outage is untracked or escalation contact is stale.

controls.reason: Every registered billing scope can be checked for configured cost alerts and a versioned runaway-resource protection policy.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A billing account without an alert or resource class without a bound fails the exact configuration join.

controls.reason: Inventory, scope and rotation records cannot prove inclusion of every infrastructure credential and machine identity or correct least-privilege scope.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known identities can pass while a hidden bootstrap credential remains broad and never rotates.

controls.reason: Prohibiting privileged execution and host access unless approved is universal across all identities, interfaces and emergency paths.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Policy checks can pass while a debug endpoint or inherited node role grants unapproved host access.

controls.reason: Upgrade-rehearsal occurrence does not prove complete node, cluster, control-plane, version, rollback or failure-path coverage.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A standard upgrade drill can pass while a mixed-version control-plane rollback fails.

controls.reason: A storage failure and restoration test is one observation without complete storage classes, corruption modes, datasets and integrity oracles.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A volume-loss drill can restore sample files while a database consistency failure remains untested.

controls.reason: Regional failover meeting availability objectives is a runtime behavior claim over provider failures, traffic and shared dependencies.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A simulated failover can meet RTO while a regional identity dependency prevents failover in production.

controls.reason: Trace propagation across every trusted service boundary requires a complete boundary and execution-path inventory.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Registered HTTP calls can propagate trace context while an asynchronous or retry path silently drops it.

controls.reason: Structured, searchable and consistently leveled logs are qualitative and universal over every writer, format, store and query path.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known schemas can validate while a plugin emits unstructured logs or critical errors use an inappropriate level.

controls.reason: Auditing seven security-sensitive action families requires complete API, background-job, admin and data-access path coverage.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Configured events can pass while a sensitive export through an uninstrumented integration leaves no audit record.

controls.reason: Monitoring four telemetry-pipeline risks cannot prove complete pipeline coverage or detect manipulation that also disables its monitor.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All dashboards can exist while an unregistered shard backlogs or quota exhaustion suppresses both telemetry and heartbeat.

controls.reason: Simulated-incident test occurrence does not prove dashboards, alerts and queries work for all incidents, permissions, data loss and timing states.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A known outage scenario can pass while an incident that breaks the telemetry source leaves diagnostics useless.

controls.reason: Every alert in the authoritative registry can be required to link at least one of six exact user, SLO, integrity, security, fraud or capacity-risk categories.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An alert with no impact-category link fails the finite registry constraint.

controls.reason: Every registered alert can be joined to an accountable owner identity and a current diagnostic or mitigation runbook.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A missing owner or runbook produces an exact referential-integrity failure.

controls.reason: Routing and escalation test occurrence cannot prove every alert, responder schedule, provider and failure mode routes correctly.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A test page can reach on-call while a real high-severity route loops or escalates to a stale contact.

controls.reason: Required responder access and tools depend on complete incident-task analysis and actual permission and tool availability under failure.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All listed responders can have roles and tools while a necessary console or emergency permission is missing during an incident.

controls.reason: For every registered SLO, exact fast- and slow-burn alert formulas can be validated against the versioned objective and window policy.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An SLO lacking either burn-rate detector or using the wrong objective value fails the finite formula join.

controls.reason: True independence and operation of a monitoring or paging failure signal require dependency and correlated-failure analysis plus execution evidence.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A heartbeat alert can exist while sharing the failed paging provider and therefore never reaches responders.

controls.reason: Every runbook can be checked for the eight exact symptoms, impact, diagnosis, containment, change, recovery, verification and escalation sections.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A runbook missing recovery verification or escalation fails the finite document schema.

controls.reason: Availability of dashboards, consoles, credentials and documentation during arbitrary incidents is an empirical correlated-failure claim.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All four can work in a routine drill while a shared identity outage makes every recovery resource inaccessible.

controls.reason: The drill ledger can require completed, version-bound events for the three exact on-call, alerting and runbook drill types.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A missing runbook drill or a drill against an obsolete process version fails the finite occurrence record.

controls.reason: Criticality and complete discovery of services, journeys, data, dependencies and manual operations require business-impact judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All five sections can exist while an indirect manual recovery step or critical journey is omitted.

controls.reason: Defining RPO for every stateful system requires a complete system inventory and correct statefulness classification.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All cataloged stateful services can have RPOs while an unregistered queue or cache with critical state is omitted.

controls.reason: Critical-journey identification and complete journey inventory are contextual and cannot be proved by the RTO register.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Every recorded critical journey can have an RTO while a support or recovery journey is missing.

controls.reason: Backup schedule and monitor checks cannot prove every required data set and backup path runs at the right cadence and succeeds.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Registered jobs can be green while an untracked data store is never backed up or a corrupt backup reports success.

controls.reason: A recovery plan can be checked for the seven exact DNS, certificate, secret, identity, network, integration and communication-system sections.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Omitting external integrations or certificates fails the finite plan schema.

controls.reason: Integrity checks and reconciliation require complete restored datasets and authoritative correctness oracles, not merely a successful command.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Checksums can match copied files while logical database relationships are inconsistent or records are missing from the manifest.

controls.reason: For a bounded recovery experiment, measured RTO and RPO can be compared exactly with versioned approved numeric objectives.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A test whose actual recovery time or point exceeds its objective fails the numeric threshold comparison.

controls.reason: Failover and failback test occurrence does not establish complete regions, versions, data states, traffic patterns and correctness oracles.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A normal drill can pass while failback after writes in both regions loses data.

controls.reason: A load test cannot prove disaster-recovery capacity for every required workload, failure combination and scaling constraint.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The test carries nominal demand while a peak recovery backlog or provider quota makes real capacity insufficient.

controls.reason: Absence of single-person, device, credential or provider dependencies requires a complete recovery dependency graph and correlated-failure proof.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Two operators can be listed while both rely on one hardware token issuer or unavailable provider.

controls.reason: Continuity procedures can be checked for four finite sections covering customer support, communication, essential manual operations and decision authority.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A continuity plan without manual operations or decision authority fails the exact document schema.

controls.reason: An error-budget policy can be versioned and timestamped before the first exhaustion event for its SLO.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A policy created after exhaustion or lacking an effective date fails the temporal rule.

controls.reason: Each SLO can require approved fast- and slow-burn formulas with exact windows and thresholds tied to its objective.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A missing chronic-risk alert or mismatched burn threshold fails the finite policy calculation.

controls.reason: An end-to-end objective model can require an explicit contribution definition for every registered dependency edge.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A dependency without an objective contribution or using another service's SLO identity fails the graph schema.

controls.reason: Release policy can maintain distinct integrity and safety gate states and prohibit averaging either into the availability score.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A failing safety gate cannot be offset by high availability under the exact gate formula.

controls.reason: User and contractual semantics for planned maintenance require product and legal interpretation; a numeric calculation can consistently encode the wrong meaning.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A metric can exclude maintenance while the customer contract counts it as downtime, yet the configured formula still passes.

controls.reason: Raw measurement inputs and calculation code can be content-addressed, preserved and replayed to reproduce the published result exactly.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A missing input or calculation mismatch fails the bounded reproducibility check.

controls.reason: Eight fields can validate entries, but a service catalog cannot prove it includes every actual operational service and dependency.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All rows can be complete while a shadow production service remains outside the catalog.

controls.reason: A support policy can define the six exact channel, severity, response, escalation, entitlement and communication expectation sections.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Omitting entitlement or escalation rules fails the finite policy schema.

controls.reason: Identity verification before every sensitive disclosure or change is a security property across complete support and administration paths.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The standard support form can verify identity while a phone escalation or integration changes sensitive data without it.

controls.reason: A case-management schema can assign six distinct request types while preserving explicit typed links among related cases.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Merging a privacy request into a defect or losing its incident link violates the enum and relation constraints.

controls.reason: Impact, urgency and consistent priority assignment require contextual assessment of varied users, harms and incidents.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A priority matrix can be applied consistently to incorrect low impact and urgency ratings.

controls.reason: Recurrence, friction and useful conversion into product or documentation signals require semantic grouping and user-experience judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Repeated requests can be split across labels and never recognized as the same friction despite complete records.

controls.reason: Every registered knowledge article can be checked for search indexing plus owner, effective version, review date and retirement state.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An article missing owner or not present in the search index fails the finite metadata and index checks.

controls.reason: A support outcome report can require the six exact quality, reopen, escalation, effort, satisfaction and recurrence measures and reject closure-only reports.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A report with closure volume but no user effort or recurrence fails the finite metric schema.

controls.reason: Accessible support and effective alternatives are user outcomes across disabilities, languages, devices and failure conditions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A channel can meet automated checks while remaining unusable to a screen-reader user or when the primary channel fails.

controls.reason: A handoff policy can define procedures for four finite contexts: time zones, teams, suppliers and incident command.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A missing supplier or incident-command handoff fails the exact policy matrix.

controls.reason: Protection according to sensitivity requires correct data classification and complete access, storage, export and retention path enforcement.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Policy records can pass while a sensitive attachment is exported to an unapproved support tool.

controls.reason: A lifecycle workflow can require a versioned service-acceptance definition before the project-to-operations transfer transition.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Transfer without acceptance criteria or with criteria dated afterward fails the temporal gate.

controls.reason: Support retirement can require an approved lifecycle-policy state and immutable communication evidence before obligations close.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A retirement without policy authorization or stakeholder communication cannot pass the state-transition gate.

controls.reason: An incident policy can define six exact criteria, severity, authority, roles, communication and escalation sections before any incident event.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A policy missing decision authority or created after an incident fails the schema or temporal rule.

controls.reason: Each incident can require a named command identity and exactly one authoritative append-only timeline.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Multiple competing authoritative timelines or missing command identity violate the finite incident schema.

controls.reason: The incident state machine can block recovery declaration until five exact journey, integrity, backlog, dependency and monitoring verification states pass.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A recovery declaration with an unchecked dependency or nonempty unapproved backlog fails the transition guard.

controls.reason: Monitoring cannot prove detection of every recurrence and delayed effect without complete symptom, time-horizon and telemetry coverage.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Dashboards can stay green while a latent corruption appears after the configured observation window.

controls.reason: Several durations are computable, but recurrence, action effectiveness and learning require causal and qualitative interpretation.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All six metrics can be present while an ineffective action is marked complete and no real learning changes practice.

controls.reason: A capacity forecast package can require seven exact ordinary, peak, seasonal, launch, growth, recovery and abuse demand scenarios.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Omitting recovery or abuse demand fails the finite scenario schema; forecast accuracy is not inferred.

controls.reason: Tracking ten resource-limit classes requires a complete component, provider and control-plane inventory that limit records cannot prove.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All known quotas can be present while an indirect database or third-party limit remains untracked.

controls.reason: Numeric forecast comparison is bounded, but updating the correct assumptions requires causal demand and model judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Actual demand can be compared while the wrong assumption is edited and the real growth driver remains unchanged.

controls.reason: Four capacity test labels do not prove complete workloads, failure domains, scaling states or correctness and stability outcomes.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Scale-up and zone-loss tests can pass separately while rebalancing during loss overloads a queue.

controls.reason: Preventing autoscaling from overwhelming every database or external dependency is a runtime safety claim over open workloads and provider limits.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A standard load test can pass while a burst scaling event exhausts a hidden third-party quota.

controls.reason: An overload policy can define the six exact admission, queuing, backpressure, prioritization, degradation and shedding mechanisms.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A service policy missing load shedding or prioritization fails the finite schema.

controls.reason: A service dashboard definition can require the six exact latency, throughput, error, queue-age, resource and unit-cost signals in one versioned view.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A view lacking unit cost or queue age fails the finite signal contract.

controls.reason: Detecting all leaks and gradual degradation requires complete endurance durations, platforms, resources, baselines and telemetry oracles.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An endurance test can pass for hours while a weekly leak or uninstrumented resource continues degrading.

controls.reason: A growth plan can be checked for five finite storage, index, log, backup and retention forecast sections.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A plan lacking backup or retention growth fails the exact schema.

controls.reason: Complete supplier limits, contract lead times and correct capacity coordination require external contract interpretation and provider inventory.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All known limits can be scheduled while an indirect provider quota or contractual notice period is missed.

controls.reason: Documentation and authorization are bounded, but proving every emergency capacity action is reversible requires empirical rollback and side-effect coverage.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An approved runbook can exist while an emergency database resize cannot be rolled back without data migration.

controls.reason: Capacity verification after five change types requires complete change detection, representative load and failure scenarios, and exact oracles.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known changes can trigger tests while an indirect dependency or data-shape shift is missed.

controls.reason: Model and test edits are observable, but whether they embody the performance-incident lesson requires causal and technical judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Both artifacts can change while the mistaken capacity assumption that caused the incident remains.

controls.reason: Recovery and SLO headroom needs plus whether cost is the sole decision motive require operational and human decision judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A capacity record can exceed a formula while an omitted recovery workload makes real headroom inadequate, or rationale hides cost pressure.

controls.reason: A cost ledger can require nine distinct fixed, variable, shared, support, data, network, license, supplier and incident categories.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Combining supplier and license cost or omitting incident cost violates the finite category schema.

controls.reason: A cost forecast can require seven exact base, growth, launch, seasonal, failure, backup and recovery scenarios.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A forecast missing failure or recovery cost fails the finite scenario manifest.

controls.reason: Budgets and alerts are inspectable, but ensuring cost controls never silently terminate any critical service is a universal runtime property.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A configured safeguard can pass while a provider budget action disables an unregistered critical workload.

controls.reason: Idle, orphaned, overprovisioned, underutilized, duplicate and forgotten status require thresholds, ownership semantics and complete resource discovery.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known resources can be classified while a shadow idle instance is absent or a critical standby is wrongly called unused.

controls.reason: A FinOps review record can require the five exact transfer, storage-tier, retention, logging and high-cardinality telemetry cost sections.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Omitting retention or network-transfer analysis fails the finite review schema.

controls.reason: An investment cost model can require the five exact labor, complexity, support, migration and lock-in categories in addition to provider invoices.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A model with invoice-only cost or missing migration labor fails the finite category check.

controls.reason: Complete supplier price changes and quota interactions require changing external feeds, contract interpretation and dependency inventory.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A review can cover known price sheets while a tier interaction or indirect supplier quota remains missed.

controls.reason: Savings attribution and detection of all shifted costs require a complete cost boundary and causal economic analysis.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Provider spend can fall while labor and network cost rise outside the measured account, producing a false savings pass.

controls.reason: Exit-criteria state is bounded, but removing every temporary launch and migration resource requires a complete resource inventory.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known temporary capacity can be deleted while a forgotten reserved instance or queue remains.

controls.reason: Every policy-tagged major architecture or procurement decision can be required to link a versioned cost-evidence package.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A major decision without cost evidence or linked to another version fails the registry join.

controls.reason: An inventory cannot prove authoritative completeness across nine open-world asset and dependency classes.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All rows can be correct while a shadow domain, certificate, device or service remains undiscovered.

controls.reason: Each asset-inventory row can be checked for nine exact owner, purpose, environment, criticality, data, exposure, version, support and retirement fields.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A row missing exposure or support status fails the finite schema; inventory completeness is not inferred.

controls.reason: Tracking six date classes depends on complete asset, vendor, certificate, key and contract inventories plus current external information.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All registered dates can be valid while an unknown certificate or contract deadline is absent.

controls.reason: Risk-based patch targets require security judgment, and deployed-version verification depends on a complete asset inventory and all deployment paths.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known assets can meet target while an unsupported production copy remains unpatched and undiscovered.

controls.reason: Every compensating-control record can require owner, monitoring, expiry and replacement plan before approval.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A control lacking an expiry or replacement plan fails the finite exception schema.

controls.reason: Preventing unsupported assets from silently remaining dependencies requires complete runtime dependency and restored-system discovery.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Catalog and scans can pass while an offline job or restored appliance still depends on an unsupported component.

controls.reason: Four compatibility test categories do not define complete versions, rollback states, datasets or correctness and recovery oracles.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known mixed-version tests can pass while rollback after a schema write corrupts older readers.

controls.reason: Monitoring failed, partial and reverted patches cannot prove complete patch-path instrumentation or correct state classification.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Dashboards can show known deployments while a disconnected device partially patches without reporting.

controls.reason: Complete removal of obsolete packages, services, accounts, ports and capabilities requires asset discovery and contextual obsolescence decisions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known obsolete items can be removed while a compiled package or forgotten account persists.

controls.reason: An incident-investigation schema can require exact patch-state and asset-state evidence references.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An investigation missing deployed patch version or affected asset identity fails the finite evidence schema.

controls.reason: Duplicate and orphaned status requires semantic equivalence, ownership and complete asset discovery before retirement.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A retirement job can remove known duplicates while a hidden orphan persists or two distinct assets are wrongly merged.

controls.reason: A decommissioning record can require eight exact owner, scope, dependency, customer, user, data, contract and completion-criteria fields.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A retirement plan missing customer impact or completion criteria fails the finite schema.

controls.reason: Essential capability and adequacy of replacement or continuity plans require operational judgment beyond a confirmation record.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A plan can be approved before shutdown while it cannot handle a critical workload or failure mode.

controls.reason: Complete inventory of ten inbound, outbound, identity, supplier and data-copy classes cannot be proved by the decommission record itself.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All sections can be populated while a hidden scheduled job, certificate or archived data copy remains.
